# Word Bocce

> A lawn game played in meaning-space: add and subtract words to roll your ball up to the jack.

By David Reinstein (https://www.davidreinstein.org/). More projects: https://projects.davidreinstein.org/

Free, in the browser, no sign-up. Source: https://github.com/daaronr/word2vecgames

## How it works

- Word arithmetic on word embeddings, as in "king - man + woman = queen". The yellow jack is a target word; your ball starts as another word. Add and subtract word tiles from your hand to move it closer.
- Distance is shown as rank: #12 means the target is the 12th-nearest word to where your ball stopped. #1 is a "bacio", a kiss on the jack.
- After every throw, "Why?" explains what each word contributed: its share of the ball's similarity to the target, and which words crowd the target before and after.

## Two word sets ("maps of meaning")

- Common sense (default): ConceptNet Numberbatch 19.08, which blends text statistics with a knowledge base of everyday facts. About 21,000 everyday words. Courts are only dealt if the best throw can be explained word by word.
- Raw text: GloVe 6B, 100 dimensions, learned only from which words appear together in Wikipedia and news text (about 40,000 words). The classic word embedding, which can surprise.

## Modes

- Daily: one court a day, the same for everyone; four balls, best one counts; shareable emoji summary.
- Practice: endless freshly dealt courts.
- Puzzles: hand-made courts with star ratings.
- Versus: against a bot or a friend on one device, with bocce scoring (first to 5), or online with up to six friends in a shared room (browser to browser; nothing is stored).

## Pages

- [Word Bocce](https://wordbocce.davidreinstein.org/): the game.
- [Teaching with Word Bocce](https://wordbocce.davidreinstein.org/teach.html): a 30-45 minute lesson plan on word embeddings for intro NLP, machine learning and data-science classes, and curious high-school classes. Covers word arithmetic, the "Why?" panel (an exact breakdown of each throw, which is not an explanation of the model), comparing the two word sets, discussion questions on bias and interpretability, and caveats (static word embeddings, not a transformer's internals).
- [Word Bocce - Game Presentation](https://wordbocce.davidreinstein.org/presentation.html): an older slide deck explaining word embeddings and an earlier multiplayer version of the game.
